messages.subject: corresponding table between gene and probeset
parts:
Hi Mark,

I am using full CDF file: HuEx-1_0-st-v2,full,A20070914,EP.cdf
In CDF file, one probeset belongs to only one gene.
now I want find a probeset belong to which gene.

can I get a table like below?
probesetID geneName
XXXXXXXX XXXXXXXX
XXXXXXXX XXXXXXXX
...


J.

messages.author: 43e2e19dd6bd2992
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] corresponding table between gene and probeset
parts:
Hi Jay,
If you use extractDataFrame() on your chip effects, you can ask for this
information to be included (addNames=T). Or you can get this information
from the cdf; for example,

cdfEnsbMono<-AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType(paste("HuEx-1_0-st-v2,U-Ensembl47,G-Affy",
"monocell",sep=","))
ugcMapEnsb<-getUnitGroupCellMap(cdfEnsbMono)
ugNamesEnsb <- getUnitGroupNamesFromUgcMap(cdfEnsbMono,ugcMapEnsb)

Then ugNamesEnsb will have this information. This can take a long time
(many minutes) the first time -- but not impossible, I ran it on my
laptop. If you just want a few units, you can also give that as an
option to getUnitGroupCellMap(). This is assuming you have already run
your plm so that you have a 'monocell' version of the Ensembl cdf (which
is created during the fitting process if it doesn't already exist; you
can check in you annotationData folder to see if it's there)

Best,
Elizabeth

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: corresponding table between gene and probeset
parts:
Hi Jay,
I didn't notice that you said you were using the full annotation -- i.e.
Affy's transcript clusters. I was talking about the Ensembl annotation,
which is roughly the size of the 'core' probesets. So the technique
below might take much longer. On the other hand, you can just use the
Affy annotation available online which is how I create the cdf. Just
make sure you get the equivalent version or they won't correspond.
Best,
Elizabeth
